edits.before: Q-bloom the pair — bot's formations eat the triple pop beautifully.
edits.after: Q-E poke owns level 1 — a toolless Rakan has no way to trade back.

edits.before: Clone games begin: the lane's information war opens in your favor.
edits.after: AoE poke widens it: your zone threat outpaces his melee assist range.

edits.before: Pop Blossom online — the disguise plus R turns brush control into ambush law.
edits.after: Pop Blossom outpaces his double-move W — time R on his engage and you win it.

edits.before: First item: root-blooms delete and the clone sells angles.
edits.after: First item: his mobility item makes Grand Entrance land.

edits.before: Late support Neeko is the ambush: crouch the pit, pop the formation, root the scatter.
edits.after: Late, his engage-disengage dance and flank threat outscale your single burst window.

edits.before: - Rakan Grand Entrance: matchup-defining — The leap knockup starts every play — track him in fog; the E extends it. The duo’s tempo bends around it. - Keep W Shapesplitter banked for their best play. - The ultimate is a fight decision, not a habit.
edits.after: - Grand Entrance (W): 14/13/12/11/10s, down to 7s late. The knockup starts every play; his Battle Dance (E) re-cast extends the dash. - Bank your W clone for his best play. - Your R (120/105/90s) is a fight decision, not a habit.

edits.before: The leap knockup starts every play — track him in fog; the E extends it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Grand Entrance (W) is down 10-14s early — track him in fog; Battle Dance (E) extends it. Commit on cooldown, not into it.

edits.before: Q-poking with the E banked forever — the root is the threat; the bloom is just the receipt.
edits.after: Standing in Gleaming Quill range while Fey Feathers shields back the chip you're spending.
